title: scores.json
description: Stage 3 output — the curation audit log. Every keep/cut decision is recorded with its five probe scores and a one-line reason, so the whole curation is inspectable, defensible, and reproducible.

core_budget.description: The computed core size and its inputs. The core budget is a function of surviving diagnostic material, not a constant — recording it here is what makes the size reproducible and reviewable. See scoring.md for the formula.

supply.description: 2200 + 250·min(n_cost_refusal,6) + 180·min(n_projectible,7) + 140·min(n_interactional,5) + 120·min(n_variation,4). Preoccupation and stable style contribute nothing — they fill space the diagnostics earned.

ceiling.description: The corpus ceiling from coverage_map.json: 4000 if firsthand_ratio < 0.50, or total_tokens < 50k, or n_clusters < 4; 5500 if total_tokens < 250k or n_clusters < 9; else 6500.

ceiling_rule.description: Which ceiling row matched, e.g. 'firsthand_ratio<0.50' or 'total_tokens<250k'. First match wins.

budget.description: clamp(supply, 3000, ceiling). The rendered SKILL.md including frontmatter is measured against this with ±10% tolerance.

floor_triggered.description: True when supply fell below the 3000 floor. The floor is a diagnostic trigger, never a padding target: re-examine the 0.45–0.55 cut band for diagnostic classes only, check for upstream under-extraction, and failing both ship a reduced-scope core with the shortfall logged. Never top up with stable_style material to reach it.

floor_resolution.description: Required in practice when floor_triggered is true: which of the three floor steps resolved it, or that the core shipped reduced-scope. Mirrors the note in fidelity-ledger/provenance.md.

counts.description: Survivor counts by class feeding the supply term, before the budget decides how many are actually written into the core.

cluster_budgets.description: Stage 4 sizing for the clusters/*.md modules — one entry per cluster considered for a module, including any the floor rejected. Recording the rejections is the point: it turns 'this cluster did not earn a module' into an auditable decision rather than an omission. Formula and counting rules in scoring.md; compute with scripts/cluster_budget.py.

cluster_id.description: Must match an id in clusters/manifest.json.

supply.description: 600 + 90·min(n_apparatus,12) + 90·min(n_moves,12) + 85·min(n_applications,8) + 30·min(n_fragments,24) + 80 + 15·min(n_siblings,9) + 400·sqrt(words/words_firsthand). Saturates near 4775, deliberately below the ceiling.

budget.description: clamp(supply, 1800, 6000). The rendered module is measured against this with ±10% tolerance.

counts.description: Inputs to the supply term, counted off Stage 2/3 artifacts rather than estimated at write time. See the counting-rules table in scoring.md.

floor_triggered.description: True when supply fell below 1800. The floor decides whether the cluster earns a module at all, and is never a padding target: fold it into its nearest sibling module, or demote its concrete attested material (events, not concepts or expression) to fidelity-ledger/episodic.md.

floor_resolution.description: Required in practice when floor_triggered is true: which sibling absorbed it, or that it went to fidelity-ledger/episodic.md, and why.

recut_flagged.description: True when n_apparatus > 12 or n_moves > 12. A segmentation signal, not a trimming one: the cluster is carrying two registers and belongs back at Stage 1 with segment.py. Never buy the space back by deleting evidence.

actual.description: Realised module size once written. Optional and worth recording: the coefficients are calibrated on a single corpus, so realised-vs-budget pairs are all a future recalibration has to work from.

weights.description: The composite weights actually used for this run. Defaults: projectibility 0.30, cost_refusal 0.25, expressive_match 0.20, interactional 0.15, preoccupation 0.10. Should sum to 1.0 after any auto-weighting and renormalisation.

weight_notes.description: Why the weights differ from the defaults, or a note that they do not — e.g. 'dialogue_ratio 0.35 → interactional 0.15 (unchanged)'. Record every change so the run stays reproducible.

composite.description: Weighted sum of scores. The hard deletion rule cuts anything below 0.55 — but note that an element above 0.55 is still cut unconditionally if it introduces generic language, forces meta-commentary, or conflicts with a higher-scoring core voice feature.

decision.description: Where the element landed. 'core' entries fill core_budget.budget by class priority first, then composite within class.

rank.description: Position within the core after class-priority ranking. Present only when decision is 'core'.

reason.description: One line. Why this element was kept or cut.

decisions.reason: incentive-vs-characteristic divergence attested in 3 clusters; predicts well
bare sentence-length average; generic; below threshold
